answer: Forge each new identity through a spiral of rising checks instead of granting full rights at once. An agent starts with tiny, reversible tasks, and only after independent peers verify that work does it climb toward the summit of voting and payment rights. Each step costs time, computation, and a small refundable deposit that is slashed on fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore pay that full climb separately for every fake identity, so creating thousands of copies becomes far more expensive than the influence any one copy can buy.
